description:
Five little pixel games, made with Claude Opus 5.5, and not one image file in the whole project. Every pixel is drawn by code. The repo is open source, so I opened it up: how the games are built, the shared 343-line engine, the 10 visual rules behind the look (I switched five of them off so you can see what each one does), and how to add your own game.

Which game would you play first? And what tiny world would you build? Tell me in the comments.

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:16 The post
0:39 The five games
1:25 Inside the repo
1:50 The engine
2:32 The 10 visual rules (switched off)
3:41 Credit + license
4:02 What people built
4:21 Make your own game
4:48 The prompt
4:55 Outro

The repo: github.com/amirmushichge/pixel-plays
Play the games: pixel-plays-ruby.vercel.app

The prompt (swap the [brackets] for your own idea)
Clone github.com/amirmushichge/pixel-plays. Read README.md and engine.js first. Add a new game: [a fisherman casting from a wooden pier]. One small place floating on white, one readable physical action, and follow every visual rule in the README. Add it to GAMES in shell.js. Leave the music out, or use your own.

About the "rule off" demos: these come from my own local copy of the repo, with one line of engine.js changed per rule, recorded at the same moment as the original. They are not part of the repo.

License: the code is MIT. The game music was made with Suno and is NOT licensed for reuse (see MUSIC.md in the repo), so it is muted in this video.
